exposure: Mode of birth (vaginal delivery, caesarean section)
cohort: The study included 200 women, 100 who delivered vaginally and 100 via caesarean section, all with vertex presentation babies weighing less than 2.5kg.
finding: While outcomes for both modes of delivery were generally similar, infants delivered by caesarean section had a higher rate of NICU admissions and longer duration of NICU stay.
mod_finding: Infants born via caesarean section had higher rates of NICU admission and longer NICU stays compared to those born vaginally, despite similar overall mortality and other neonatal morbidities.
birth_weight: Less than 2.5kg (mean 2.26kg in CS group, 2.3kg in vaginal delivery group)
